posts.author: *Walter Bloomberg
posts.text:
US INFLATION COMES IN HOTTER THAN EXPECTED IN OCTOBER

US headline CPI rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% forecast, while core CPI increased 0.3% versus 0.2% expected.

Food prices jumped 0.5%, energy rose 0.7%, and gasoline climbed 1.0%.

Housing costs increased 0.3%, while real earnings for private-sector workers were unchanged.

The hotter-than-expected inflation report strengthens the case for further Fed rate hikes.
posts.ko: 10월 CPI 세부: 식품 +0.5%, 에너지 +0.7%, 휘발유 +1.0%, 주거 +0.3% — 추가 인상 근거 강화

posts.author: *Walter Bloomberg
posts.text:
US CORE INFLATION ACCELERATES TO HIGHEST LEVEL SINCE JANUARY 2025

US core CPI accelerated to 3.7% annualized over the past three months, its highest reading since January 2025.

Supercore inflation surged to 5.5% annualized, the strongest pace since April 2024, up from 4.6% in September.

Meanwhile, the six-month core CPI rate eased to 2.7% from 2.9%.

An unofficial estimate puts annual core inflation at 2.74%, up from 2.56%.

FED COULD ACCELERATE RATE HIKES AFTER HOT INFLATION REPORT

The Fed may face a choice between a 50-basis-point hike in December or back-to-back increases in December and January, according to WSJ's Nick Timiraos.

Core CPI rose 0.3% in October, beating expectations and marking the third consecutive monthly increase of that size.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller warned that another hot reading could justify a 50bps hike, though other officials have yet to endorse the move.

The inflation report raises the likelihood of additional rate hikes in 2027.

posts.author: The Kobeissi Letter
posts.text:
Rate hike expectations are soaring.

In a sudden turn of events, markets are now pricing in the possibility of a 50 basis point rate hike in December.

Market expectations for a 50 basis point hike have surged to 11%, while expectations for a 25 basis point hike stand at 84%.

It is no longer a matter of if the Fed will hike rates in December, but rather by how much.
